title: The Daily Five
dek: Five questions on Maccabi's Moscow triumph, a landmark gymnastics ruling, cup draws and an Israeli closing in on a Premier League move.

questions.question: On 8 May 2005, who was named Final Four MVP after sparking a decisive 7-0 run as Maccabi Tel Aviv beat Tau Cerámica Vitoria 90–78 in Moscow to retain the EuroLeague title?
questions.explanation: Jasikevičius scored 22 points with 6 rebounds and 5 assists in the final and was named 2005 Final Four MVP.

questions.question: A Tel Aviv magistrate's court ordered the Israel Gymnastics Federation, the Olympic Committee of Israel and the Wingate Institute to pay two former national-team gymnasts a combined sum for shoulder injuries sustained during training between 2008 and 2016. Roughly how much in total?
questions.explanation: The court ordered a combined roughly 1.6 million shekels, split into 1,118,000 shekels for the first gymnast and 505,000 shekels for the second.

questions.question: In the Toto Cup semi-final draw, who will Hapoel Tel Aviv face on Sunday, August 16?
questions.explanation: Hapoel Tel Aviv were drawn against Ironi Kiryat Shmona, with both semi-finals kicking off simultaneously at 20:00 on August 16.

questions.question: Israel international Manor Solomon, fresh off a prolific loan season at Leeds United, is closing in on a permanent move from Tottenham Hotspur to which club?
questions.explanation: Solomon is expected to sign a three-year contract, with a club option for a fourth season, at West Ham United.

questions.question: If Maccabi Tel Aviv beat CSKA Sofia in Europa League third qualifying round, who is their confirmed playoff-round opponent?
questions.explanation: Maccabi Tel Aviv's official website confirmed OFI Crete as their playoff-round opponent, with legs on August 20 and 27.
